metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully applied strikethrough to the last paragraph of GEOG2169_Course_Outline_2022-23.docx using Format > Text > Strikethrough, then saved with Ctrl+S.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select paragraphs in LibreOffice Writer and apply strikethrough formatting via Format > Text > Strikethrough menu.
metadata.task_rationale: Extended scope version of the original task: the same strikethrough formatting operation is applied to TWO paragraphs (first and last) instead of just one. Tests whether the agent can repeat the formatting operation on a different paragraph in the same session.
metadata.explanation: Agent must apply strikethrough to both the first and last content paragraphs. Getter reads saved .docx and checks runs in each paragraph; metric awards 0.5 per paragraph. Initial state has no strikethrough on either paragraph. [Fixed: replaced invalid 8-char MD5 suffix '9e7abe4b' with proper 32-char MD5 hash 'd8440cb16db3c65fff5a2b530ef73072' computed from '72b810ef-4156-4d09-8f08-a0cf57e7cefe|4']

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the saved .docx file after postconfig saves it with Ctrl+S, ensuring fresh state.
Getter filters non-empty paragraphs and correctly identifies first (content_paras[0]) and last (content_paras[-1]) paragraphs, matching the instruction's 'both the first and last paragraphs'.
Strikethrough check uses all(bool(r.font.strike) for r in runs) requiring all runs in the paragraph to have explicit strike formatting set.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('first_para_strike') and expected.get('last_para_strike') without nesting under 'rules' key.
Partial credit logic (0.5 per paragraph) is semantically appropriate for this two-subgoal task.
Error handling returns {'error': ...} on missing file, and metric returns 0.0 on error.

Minor issue: r.font.strike returns None (not False) when formatting is inherited from a style rather than set directly on the run. bool(None) is False, so style-inherited strikethrough would produce a false negative. For LibreOffice UI-applied formatting this is typically direct run formatting, so low practical risk.

Minor ambiguity: 'first paragraph of the course outline' is interpreted as the first non-empty paragraph in doc.paragraphs (which may be a title/heading). This is a reasonable interpretation given the document structure.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To handle style-inherited strikethrough, consider checking both r.font.strike and the paragraph's style strikethrough. For example: use r.font.strike is not False (treats None as potentially inherited True) or check paragraph-level style. However, for typical UI-applied formatting via LibreOffice this is not a blocking issue.

If the 'first paragraph' should specifically be the first body paragraph (excluding title/headings), add a filter for paragraph style (e.g., skip paragraphs with style name starting with 'Heading' or 'Title').
